- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion or rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overreacts and forecasts continued rise; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or apply lag correction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or apply downward bias in second half of horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates in early days (1–7) when sentiment is positive; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.67/1.00 patterns, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply smoothing or reduce volatility weight in forecast.
